title: First-Touch-to-Activation 12-Week Micro-Sprints
body:
Purpose:
A compact, experiment-oriented onboarding template aimed at getting customers from first touch to measurable activation within 12 weeks using 1–2 week micro-sprints. Designed for mid-market accounts and technical buyers integrating Redwood (hosted / dedicated / private). The doc is intentionally pragmatic — lots of checklists, quick hypotheses, and specific signals tied to renewal risk.

Audience:
- Customer Success Managers (primary)
- Solutions Engineers (SE)
- Onboarding Engineers (dedicated/private installs)
- Account Execs for renewal-awareness

Quick overview (one-liner):
Run four 3-week cycles (broken into 1–2 week micro-sprints) with outcome-driven deliverables: First value, Integration baseline, Feature adoption experiments, Scale & renewal prep.

Sprint cadence and playbook (granular)
Week 0 (pre-kickoff, owner: SE):
- Verify access: API keys, network allowlists, KMS access (if Private).
- Pre-load sample config for quick demo (model, seq len, token limits).
- Slack channel + calendar invites created.
- TODO: confirm telemetry endpoints from app team (events we can track).

Micro-sprint A (Weeks 1–2): Kickoff + Quick Wins (owned by CSM + SE)
Goals (success definition):
- Customer able to call API and get a valid response in dev environment.
- First simple integration path implemented (e.g., support bot, summary endpoint).
Success metrics (activation events):
- API success rate >= 95% (first 48 hours)
- 3 successful end-to-end calls by customer devs
- First dashboard event: "first_model_response" recorded in telemetry
Deliverables/checklist:
- Shared runbook: how-to-run-local-tests (SE)
- Demo recording of the workflow for internal stakeholders
- Open ticket for any auth/network errors (tag: onboard/auth)
Common blockers & playbooks:
- Auth failure -> run quick-check script -> escalate to infra if IP blocked
- Model mismatch (unexpected output) -> create prompt-iteration ticket, propose function-calling as a fix

Micro-sprint B (Weeks 3–4): Integration baseline + SLA guardrails (owned by Onboarding Eng)
Goals:
- Integration running on staging with baseline load (x calls/min as agreed)
- Latency baseline and cost estimate captured
Success metrics:
- 95th pct latency measured for 512-token requests
- Cost estimate per daily active user (sample calculation)
- Baseline accuracy figure for core flow (manual eval pass rate >= 70%)
Deliverables:
- Load test report (attach sheet link)
- Implementation notes: batching, caching guidance applied
- Observability hooks deployed (tracing + error tagging)
Risk signals and thresholds (auto flags):
- Latency > 2x target for two consecutive days -> tag as performance-risk
- Cost per 1k tokens > budgeted -> cost-risk

Micro-sprint C (Weeks 5–8): Feature adoption experiments (owned by CSM + Product Advocate)
Approach: run 3 small experiments to nudge users towards higher-value features (e.g., streaming, function-calling, embeddings for search). Each experiment = hypothesis, implementation, measure window (2 weeks).
Example experiments:
- Experiment 1: Enable streaming for interactive agent -> hypothesis: UX time-to-first-token improves NPS for support reps by 10%
- Experiment 2: Swap to quantized model variant for background batch jobs -> hypothesis: cost drops 30% with <3% quality regression
- Experiment 3: Embed-based search pilot for KB -> hypothesis: query resolution rate improves by 15%
Metrics to capture:
- Feature adoption rate (users invoking feature / total DAUs)
- Quality regressions (sampled evals, flag rate)
- Business metrics tied to feature (e.g., resolved tickets/day)
Playbook notes:
- If quality regression > threshold -> rollback model variant -> create postmortem
- If feature adoption < 10% after two weeks -> run short user interview list

Micro-sprint D (Weeks 9–12): Scale, handoff, and renewal triggers (owned by CSM + AE)
Goals:
- Product in production for core flow with clear SLA expectations
- Renewal signals assembled and executive summary drafted
Deliverables:
- Production runbook (ops + escalation paths)
- Renewal signal dashboard (sheet + shared Confluence page)
- Executive 1-pager: success, risks, ask for next term
Renewal signals (positive):
- Sustained MAU growth > 20% month-over-month since week 6
- Feature adoption meeting business target (as agreed in contract)
- NPS or CSAT > target for power users
Renewal risk flags (examples):
- Churn cue A: API errors > 3% for billing-critical routes for 5+ days
- Churn cue B: Support backlog > 10 outstanding P0s
- Churn cue C: Customer not using paid feature X for 30 days post-launch

Scorecard / KPIs (rolling):
- Activation score: binary flag when first 3 success metrics met
- Health score: composite (uptime, latency, adoption, support volume)
- Renewal likelihood (low/med/high) with qualitative notes

Communication templates (short & copy-ready)
- Week1 kickoff email subject: "Welcome — quick checklist to get your first Redwood response"
- Template body (short): Hi <Name>, wanted to confirm we've granted keys and scheduled the kickoff. Please run the attached quick-check script and paste one sample response in the Slack channel.
- Renewal outreach subject (week 10): "Executive summary + proposed roadmap for next term"
- Note: keep exec summary to 1 page, include cost delta, adoption %, and 2 asks.

Operational runbooks and tags (for triage):
- Ticket tags to use: onboard/auth, onboard/perf, onboard/quality, renew/signal
- Confluence anchors: onboard-setup, onboarding-experiments, renew-signals
- Slack shortcuts: /onboard-checklist, /raise-onboard-issue

Unresolved questions (notes-to-self):
- Should we include a separate micro-sprint for security review in Private deployments? (likely yes for regulated customers)
- What is the minimal telemetry schema we require for activation? Need to align with Product telemetry owners (PRD-telemetry-2025)
- How to automate renewal scoring from telemetry vs manual CSM input (automation proto exists but incomplete)

Short checklist for next steps (CSM owner):
1) Share this doc with SE and Onboarding Eng -> assign owners for each micro-sprint
2) Create initial telemetry list and map to activation events (sheet)
3) Spin up renewal dashboard stub and populate with historic customers for calibration
4) Pilot with 2 mid-market accounts in next 30 days

Appendix: short examples and snippets
- Quick-check curl snippet (paste into Slack): curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Minimal telemetry events: first_model_response, integration_completed, feature_X_used, error_rate_window

Notes (brevity / informal):
- Keep the pilot light-weight. We want measurable outputs fast: logs, small evals, and a yes/no activation flag.
- This is intentionally experiment-first — we prioritize data over perfect docs.
- TODO: convert this into a shareable onboarding sheet template and one-pager for AEs.

End of draft.
